stem: A 15-year-old asks why the paediatrician is asking about home, school, peers, alcohol, sex, mood, sleep, safety, spirituality, and social media during a review for abdominal pain; what is the best explanation?

options.text: These questions are only used when a doctor suspects criminal behaviour
They are part of a structured psychosocial assessment that looks at health influences across adolescent life
They replace the need for medical history and examination
They are mainly used to decide whether parents should leave the room
They are only relevant in mental health clinics

explanation: Structured adolescent psychosocial assessment is the best explanation. These questions form part of HEEADSS-style screening, which explores the home and social context, wellbeing, risk behaviours, and other influences on health across adolescence.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because these questions are part of routine adolescent assessment, not only used when criminal behaviour is suspected.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because they are part of a structured psychosocial assessment that looks at health influences across adolescent life.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because psychosocial screening complements rather than replaces the medical history and examination.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because while rooming arrangements may influence discussion, that is not the main purpose of the assessment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this assessment is relevant to general adolescent care, not only to mental health clinics.
